svg.aria-label: Architecture of one turn. At session start, after /clear and after compaction, the SessionStart hook injects the orchestrator playbook into the main thread only, registered as four parts (--part 1 to 4) of at most 9,500 characters each and staggered so they arrive in order; subagents do not receive it. When a message the user typed mentions production mode, the UserPromptSubmit hook adds one line to the main thread on how to set and unset a repository's production mark. The main thread sends a brief to a subagent, which works from its definition in agents/*.md, which sets its reasoning effort, together with CLAUDE.md and the brief, and returns a bounded report. A subagent may dispatch one layer of haiku workers for short mechanical work; a worker cannot dispatch further. Every tool call from either thread passes PreToolUse before the tool runs: it denies nested dispatch inside subagents other than a haiku worker, git commit --no-verify, Bash, Read or Grep calls that would print a secret value, direct writes to HANDOFF.md, and a researcher or retriever subagent changing, moving or deleting an existing file, while researcher and retriever subagents may still read files, run commands and create new files; a gh pr merge in a repository marked as production waits until the user approves it on the spot. While the 5-hour usage is at 95% or more, the limit pause in PreToolUse holds every call from either thread until the reset; every 50 minutes it denies the held call, the thread then makes the pause call (: 限额暂停), which is held again, and once the reset passes the call is allowed; in the main thread, the user's own input sent after usage reached 95% and the keepalive's last wake-up pass without a hold. The limit pause reads the usage from a local file that the status line wrapper writes from the rate limits Claude Code passes to the status line. A denial sends its reason back to the calling thread, which tries another way; an allowed call runs the tool. Each guard denial is appended to a local denial log, and the PermissionDenied hook appends auto-mode classifier denials to the same log without changing control flow. After the tool runs, PostToolUse returns a rule-file reminder as added context to the calling thread when a rule file was edited, and when a new worktree is entered it symlinks CLAUDE.md, node_modules and .env* from the main checkout into that worktree without replying. When the main thread tries to end the turn, the Stop hooks run, and if all pass the turn ends. Three of them are synchronous gates. The context watermark gate adds a reminder once per session over 35%, or on every turn when the session has no scratchpad, and lets the stop pass, blocks once over 40%, or on every turn when the session has no scratchpad, and after that blocks again at every further rise of 5 points over the usage at its last block; the reply gate blocks once when the reply's last sentence offers a next step; the task checklist gate blocks while the session's checklist in ~/.claude/state/checklists/<session id>.json has todo or doing items, and passes when background tasks or crons are pending, for subagents, and after 3 blocks on an unchanged checklist. A block by any of these three gates returns control to the main thread; after the checklist gate it works on the open items. After the reply gate it either takes the offered step or, when the decision really is the user's, asks again with the background, the consequences of each option and a recommendation. After the watermark gate's first block it finishes any wrap-up that the context it already holds can complete, and when a new large block of work comes next it runs the handoff skill, in which the main thread writes HANDOFF.new.md itself and finalize.sh puts it in place as HANDOFF.md, and tells the user to switch to a new session; after each further block it generates the handoff at once. A new session reads that file to carry on. Neither the reply gate nor the watermark gate blocks the turn it has just blocked and resumed, so a single attempt to stop is blocked at most once and that turn's next attempt passes; the watermark gate still blocks again in later turns as usage rises. The fourth Stop hook, the keepalive gate, never blocks the stop: it runs in the background after the turn has ended, and once the main thread's context has reached 150,000 tokens and 50 minutes pass with no new turn, it wakes the main thread to reply with only a full stop, which keeps the one-hour prompt cache warm while the user is away. Before it wakes the main thread it probes the API, and while the API is unreachable it probes again every 30 seconds until 57 minutes after it started, then gives up because a wake-up could no longer renew the cache before it expires. Each wake-up starts the next timer, until 8 hours have passed since the user's own last message; the last wake-up before that limit asks the main thread to write a handoff with the handoff skill when work is left, and otherwise to reply with only a full stop. A wake-up answered with Done stops the keepalive until the user's next message. The keepalive is also registered on SessionEnd, where it marks the session ended so that an old timer never wakes a new session.

injects the playbook part by part,
staggered so they arrive in order,

g.text: over 35%: reminds once a session, passes
5 more points: blocks again, handoff now
blocks once when the reply's last
probes the API first; offline: retries
every 30 s, gives up after 57 min
runs in the background, never blocks
until 8 h after the user's last message
last wake-up: handoff if work is left
answered Done: off until the user writes
on SessionEnd: marks the session ended,
so an old timer never wakes a new one

svg.text: sync gate blocks: back to main thread
checklist gate: work on the open items
reply gate: do the offered step
new large work next: the handoff skill
writes the handoff; suggest a new session
reply and watermark gates block once:
the resumed turn's next stop passes
or Done when finished or handed off;
the last one: handoff if work is left

g.text: deny nested dispatch other than a
calls that would print a secret value
subagents may only create new files
handoff guard: deny hand edits of HANDOFF.md
production merge gate: gh pr merge
guard denials: appended to the denial log
rule-file reminder, when a rule file
worktree links, on entering a new
worktree: symlinks on disk, no reply
holds the call until the reset;
makes the pause call, held again
blocked, sent back or woken: control returns to the thread
